subject: Cloud storefront SKU mapping and co-sell handshake

Subject: Cloud storefront SKU mapping proposal for EdgeApps / multi-cloud co-sell handshake

Hi Suzanne + marketplace teams,

Following up from our demo last week — attaching a short proposal for how Redwood could expose a small set of SKUs across AWS / Azure / GCP storefronts to support EdgeApps' rollout. The goal is: one clear entry path for SMBs, a mid-market SKU for predictable throughput, and an enterprise SKU that bundles Dedicated capacity + SSO & audit logs.

High-level proposed SKU map (draft):
- Starter: hosted API, single-region (us-east-1/us-central), token-based billing, best-effort latency (for POCs).
- Scale: hosted API, multi-region read-replica, auto-burst for traffic spikes, recommended model variant (4-bit quantized) for cost.
- Enterprise: Dedicated pool SKU, SLA-backed, VPC peering + KMS integration, region selection by customer.

Cloud-specific notes (draft):
- AWS: list Starter & Scale as Public listings; Enterprise via Private Offer (DocuSign/PO). Co-sell ask: enable Marketplace co-sell for Scale & Enterprise.
- Azure: prefer SKU names to include "Enterprise (Bring Your Own VNet)" for compliance buyers; co-sell requires partner enablement checklist.
- GCP: suggest delaying Enterprise until we validate dedicated GPU telemetry; Surface Starter and Scale first.

Open questions / asks:
1) Suzanne — any hard requirements from EdgeApps on region coverage or metered billing behavior?
2) Marketplace ops (AWS/Azure) — any technical constraints on metering granularity (per-API token vs. per-hour) that should change SKU boundaries?
3) Karthik — feasibility for a single Scale image that we can quantize differently per cloud without splitting SKUs?

Attached: initial SKU mapping spreadsheet (storefront-sku-matrix-v1.xlsx) and a short co-sell playbook outline (co-sell-playbook-notes.pdf).

If this looks reasonable I can pull this into a shared Drive doc and set a follow-up to lock decisions and owners.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber

All — quick technical note after reviewing the matrix and Suzanne's asks. High-level constraints:

- A single Scale image across clouds is doable if we standardize on a quantization profile (we've seen strong parity with 4-bit QAT in our benchmarks). But Azure/GCP driver stacks differ; we should bake image variants per cloud and keep SKU semantics identical (same billing tier).
- Region gating: Dedicated pools (Enterprise SKU) require reservation of capacity per-region. That changes lead time (2–4 weeks for enterprise-ready pools in new regions).
- Metering: AWS Metering Service supports per-API call metering via SKU-based usage dimensions, Azure prefers hourly marketplace metering for private offers (we can add a bridge layer but it affects billing reconciliation).

Recommendation: keep SKU names consistent across clouds but add a metadata tag (cloud_variant: aws/azure/gcp) for technical ops. Practically that means one public listing per cloud for Starter/Scale and a private offer entry for Enterprise.

I attached a short note with capacity implications (sku-capacity-memo.txt). Happy to sync with Marketplace ops to map metering dims to each SKU.

—Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
Attachment: sku-capacity-memo.txt (text/plain)

Heads up on ops constraints:

- AWS private offer flow: PO + pricing table mapping required. If Enterprise uses reserved GPU pools, billing reconciliation must map reserved hours to metered usage — ops effort ~1.5 engineer-weeks to build reconciliation logic unless we scope Enterprise to committed flat-fee invoices.
- Azure metering: the marketplace's hourly unit is the path of least resistance for private offers. If EdgeApps insists on per-token for Scale we will need a middleware aggregator that emits hourly reconciliations to Azure (adds latency to billing and complexity).
- GCP listing: GCP requires a different SKU ID per billing dimension (token vs. hour) — strong reason to avoid different metering primitives per cloud if we want a single SKU identity.

Recommendation:
- Starter: per-token fine (public listing)
- Scale: per-token preferred, but if Azure forces hourly, map Scale -> Scale (per-token) with a reconciliation shim for Azure only (ops risk).
- Enterprise: committed flat-fee via private offer / reserved pool.

Attachment: marketplace-metering-checklist.md (text/markdown)

—Ben
Director, Platform Operations | Redwood Inference
